newsitem.title: JAPAN: Effort needed on Okinawa before election - PM quoted.
newsitem.headline: Effort needed on Okinawa before election - PM quoted.

text.p: Efforts are needed to solve the Okinawa problem before Japan holds general elections, Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto was quoted as saying on Friday.
Economic Planning Agency Minister Shusei Tanaka said Hashimoto strongly denied a media report today that the Liberal Democratic Party was preparing for general elections to be held during October.
Hashimoto made the comment at a morning cabinet meeting, Tanaka said.
Asked about the September monthly economic report released earlier on Friday by the EPA, Tanaka said: "We are at a difficult, sensitive stage."

He said the job situation was gradually improving but further strength in the economy was yet to be seen and regional economies and small and medium-sized companies had yet to feel that business was better.
He said it was necessary to push forward with deregulation and structural reform to ensure that economic recovery continued in the medium and long term.

Hashimoto said he had "a sense of crisis" about the need for deregulation, Tanaka said. The prime minister said that deregulation was needed at a time of global economic change, citing the telecommunications and financial sectors in particular.
